title: Ethiopian Lamb Firfir
community: Ethiopia — the lamb wat sauce firfir
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Lamb Firfir — the celebration version of firfir, made with lamb wat sauce (from Ye-Beg Key Wat) tossed with torn injera, kibbeh, and berbere. More prized than beef firfir — served the morning after a celebration using the previous night's lamb sauce.
longDesc: Lamb firfir is the post-celebration morning dish — made from the previous night's lamb wat, it signals that the household has been generous enough to have lamb to spare. It is the breakfast of the day after a wedding or religious celebration in Ethiopia.
ingredients: 1 cup lamb wat sauce (ETH025 or similar)
steps: See ETH032 — substitute lamb wat sauce for beef Key Wat sauce.
chefTips: Lamb firfir is richer and more fragrant than beef firfir — the lamb fat in the sauce adds depth.
cookingScience: See ETH032 for firfir cooking science. Lamb wat sauce has a higher fat content than beef wat — this fat is absorbed by the injera more readily, producing a richer, more unctuous firfir.
sustainabilityTips: The ultimate use of celebration leftovers.
servedWith: With a soft-boiled egg for breakfast
culturalNote: Lamb firfir is the morning that proves the previous evening was truly special — the leftover lamb sauce becoming a breakfast dish of even greater character than the wat it came from.
